identity.name: Rebellion of Umar ibn Hafsun
native_names: ثورة عمر بن حفصون (Thawrat ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣūn)

land.text: the provinces of Reyyo, Elvira and Jaén that the rebels held

predecessors.note: Not a state of its own before: the rebels took the land from the Emirate of Córdoba.

successors.note: Bobastro, the last stronghold, surrendered in 928 (Abd al-Rahman III page); the rest of the rebel land had returned in 914.

capitals.name: Bobastro
capitals.note: Ibn Hafsun's fortress in the mountains of Málaga (Reyyo); the page says only that he 'moved his headquarters to Poley' around 885.

capitals.name: Poley (Aguilar de la Frontera)
capitals.note: 'Around 885, to be more centrally located so that he could more quickly respond to external threats'; defeated at Poley in 891 by Abdullah, he 'returned to Bobastro' (undated).

rulers.name: Umar ibn Hafsun
rulers.note: 'By 883, he had become the leader of the rebels'; 'Ibn Hafsun died in 917'.

rulers.name: Sons of Umar ibn Hafsun (Ja'far, Abd al-Rahman, Hafs)
rulers.note: 'Ibn Hafsun died in 917'; 'his sons Ja'far, 'Abd-ar-Rahman and Hafs tried to continue the resistance' (Ibn Hafsun page); Hafs, the last to fall, 'surrendered in 928' (Abd al-Rahman III page). The pages give no order of succession. Renamed by reviewer eu-12-a, 2026-10-25 (was 'Hafs ibn Umar' for 917-928).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 883-913: the rebel provinces. The Abdallah page says Ibn Hafsun 'conquered the provinces of Reyyo (including Bobastro), Elvira (including Granada), and Jaén'; the Ibn Hafsun page adds 'portions of the Provinces of' Cádiz and Seville. The pages give no boundary, so whole provinces are a reading (conf 2); 891 'lost several cities' and 892 'reconquered all the lost territories'. Cliopatria has no row.

New keyframe, 914-927: Bobastro and its mountains. 'By the end of 914, he had captured 70 of Ibn Hafsun's castles' (Ibn Hafsun page); the army reached Algeciras on 1 June 914 after taking Málaga (Abd al-Rahman III page). Hafs held Bobastro until 928; the extent of what the sons kept is not on the pages (conf 1).

ledger.note: 883: Umar ibn Hafsun leads the rebel south of al-Andalus. 'By 883, he had become the leader of the rebels in the provinces to the south and the west of the' capital; a homicide in c. 879 started his outlawry and he fought the emir in 882.

region.text: the Hafsunid provinces except Bobastro, and Algeciras

ledger.note: 914: the emir takes the rebel coast and the castles. Reached Algeciras on 1 June 914 after taking Málaga; 'by the end of 914, he had captured 70 of Ibn Hafsun's castles' (Ibn Hafsun page). Bobastro holds out.
928: Bobastro surrenders. Hafs, the last of Ibn Hafsun's sons, 'surrendered in 928 and had his life spared' after a six-month siege.
928: the Hafsunid rebellion ends with the fall of Bobastro. 'Hafs surrendered Bobastro in 928 and fought with the Umayyad army in' Galicia (Ibn Hafsun page).

wars.name: Revolt of Umar ibn Hafsun
wars.outcome: The rebels hold the south from 883. Ibn Hafsun is beaten at Poley in 891 but has 'reconquered all the lost territories' by 892; he converts to Christianity in 899, offers allegiance to the Fatimid Caliphate in 910, signs a peace with the emir in 911, joins the Umayyads against the northern Christians in 916 and dies in 917; the emir takes the coast in 914 and Bobastro in 928.
wars.note: The Abdallah page gives 911 for the peace and 'the war broke out again the following year'. [Reviewer eu-12-x, 2026-10-25: from moved 882 -> 883, the state's start, so the war lies inside the life; Ibn Hafsun fought the emir in 882, before he led the rebel provinces by 883]

certainty.note: Held castles and valleys rather than a bounded province; no treaty line.

sources.title: Umar ibn Hafsun
sources.note: Dates 879-928, headquarters, lands held, conversion 899, Fatimid pledge 910, death 917, Bobastro 928.

sources.title: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Umawi
sources.note: The provinces Reyyo, Elvira and Jaén; 891-892 swing; 911 peace.

sources.title: Abd al-Rahman III
sources.note: 914 coast and Algeciras, 928 surrender of Hafs.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks (rule 5), written by eu-12-a because the Emirate of Córdoba's loss and gain events name it as counterpart. Start 883 is the page's 'by 883'; the revolt itself began c. 879-880 (the page dates a homicide to 879 and a battle against the emir to 882). The land is the three provinces named on the Abdallah page, a reading: the pages give no boundary and mention only 'portions' of Cádiz and Seville. Not settled: what the sons held between 914 and 928; the 916 alliance with the Umayyads ('for a time taxes were paid') has no end date; the 910 Fatimid pledge is not a territorial relation. The Emirate dossier carries the matching loss (883) and gains (914, 928).
